items.title: Proudly Human Promises to Certify AI-Free Books
items.excerpt: Australian startup Proudly Human, founded by former chief scientist Alan Finkel, joins a growing field of services certifying books as written without AI assistance; Finkel says two of the Big Five are in talks.

items.title: 11 Books for Understanding the AI Debate
items.excerpt: As Anthropic heads toward an IPO and data centers become a political issue, PW rounds up 11 books on AI safety, risk and regulation for readers following the debate.

items.title: AAP Calls on Meta to Drop 'Onerous' Terms of Service
items.excerpt: The Association of American Publishers called Meta's new commercial terms, which would let it crawl business websites for AI training with no opt-out short of leaving its platforms, 'an appalling landgrab of unprecedented proportion.'

items.title: 'Does Meta think we can't read?' Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update

items.title: Editor's letter: Can AI predict the Booker winner? Not likely
items.excerpt: The Bookseller's editor asked AI to predict the Booker Prize winner; 'believe the hype around AI if you must, but when asked to predict the future its limitations were plain to see.'

items.title: Copyright Infringement Lawsuit Against OpenAI Draws More than 50 Amicus Briefs
items.excerpt: More than 50 amicus briefs filed in the consolidated Authors Guild v. OpenAI case map the fault lines over AI training on books, pirated sources and infringing outputs ahead of summary judgment.

items.title: From AI Adoption to AI Practice: Building Governed AI in Scholarly Publishing

items.title: What AI Can't Learn About Peer Review... Because Nobody Can Explain It
items.excerpt: Taylor & Francis's Victoria Corless argues that generative AI can summarize manuscripts and check references, but automating peer review risks losing tacit editorial expertise nobody has documented.
